title: Shiv — Listen
description: Long-form episodes from Shiv’s follow list — history, science, philosophy, and writing that repay attention. Private taste feed for Apple Podcasts.
author: Shivanshu Chaudhary

items.title: Andy Weir: Project Hail Mary Author Teaches Writing (How I Write)
items.description:
David Perell with Andy Weir on how he builds hard-science plots for The Martian and Project Hail Mary — inventing problems from real physics, then rewriting until the story earns its surprises.

Watch: https://youtu.be/1WX2hpu_-N8

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/andy-weir-project-hail-mary-author-teaches-writing/id1700171470?i=1000792387666

items.title: 367 | Jared Diamond on the Course of History and the Role of leaders
items.description:
Sean Carroll with Jared Diamond on what actually steers history — geography, institutions, and when individual leaders change the course versus when they mostly ride larger forces.

Watch: https://youtu.be/mW45xe6NdHE

Episode: https://preposterousuniverse.com/podcast/2026/09/07/367-jared-diamond-on-the-course-of-history-and-the-role-of-leaders/

items.title: Public Choice and Politics Without Romance (with Mike Munger) (EconTalk)
items.description:
Russ Roberts with Mike Munger on public choice — politics without romance, the “Munger Test” for new government powers, and why voters rationally stay uninformed.

Watch: https://youtu.be/JAEjUiEzXUY

Episode: https://www.econtalk.org/public-choice-and-politics-without-romance-with-mike-munger/

items.title: 897: Intergenerational Space Travel (This American Life)
items.description:
Stories about the gap between people born a few years apart — a wedding toast that still stings decades later, a teenage movie-theater job revisited, and a mother and daughter stuck in a morning fight over hair.

Watch: https://youtu.be/oAwH5v_u9cw

Episode: https://www.thisamericanlife.org/897/intergenerational-space-travel

items.title: How to Make a Difference: Part 2 (Hidden Brain)
items.description:
Shankar Vedantam continues with psychologist Martin Seligman on how to strengthen agency after setbacks — seeing new possibilities and trusting that your actions can still change what comes next.

Episode: https://www.hiddenbrain.org/podcast/how-to-make-a-difference-part-2/

items.title: AI researchers debate how close we are to recursive self-improvement (Dwarkesh Podcast)
items.description:
Dwarkesh Patel with John Schulman, Beren Millidge, and Charlie O’Neill on how close frontier labs are to AI systems that can improve themselves — and what that would change.

Watch: https://youtu.be/PrSf7IOYu-I

Episode: https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/john-beren-charlie

items.title: 709. The Terror: The Execution of Marie Antoinette (Part 3) (The Rest Is History)
items.description:
Tom Holland and Dominic Sandbrook on Marie Antoinette’s year in prison after Louis XVI’s execution, the factions that argued over her fate, and how she met the guillotine on 16 October 1793.

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-terror-the-execution-of-marie-antoinette-part-3/id1537788786?i=1000789800237

items.title: Mark Normand: How to Make Your Writing More Funny (How I Write)
items.description:
Mark Normand on how he learned to write comedy after arriving in New York as a nobody — joke construction, bombing, and getting funny on the page.

Watch: https://youtu.be/oXxwMLPZOZE

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/mark-normand-how-to-make-your-writing-more-funny-how-i-write/id1700171470?i=1000792026873

items.title: What Humans, Animals and Plants Tell Us About Consciousness | Michael Pollan (Huberman Lab)
items.description:
Andrew Huberman with Michael Pollan on consciousness across humans, animals, and plants — what science can say about subjective experience, and where the hard problem still resists.

Watch: https://youtu.be/nk15CT41MFc

Episode: https://www.hubermanlab.com/episode/what-humans-animals-and-plants-tell-us-about-consciousness-michael-pollan

items.title: 369 | Gregg Caruso on Living Well Without Free Will (Sean Carroll's Mindscape)
items.description:
Sean Carroll with philosopher Gregg Caruso on hard incompatibilism: why he rejects free will, what that means for blame and criminal justice, and how to keep love, choice, and responsibility without desert.

Watch: https://youtu.be/mQBnjImNOm0

Episode: https://preposterousuniverse.com/podcast/2026/09/28/369-gregg-caruso-on-living-well-without-free-will/

items.title: Noam Brown – Agent swarms, alignment, & recursive self-improvement (Dwarkesh Podcast)
items.description:
Dwarkesh Patel with OpenAI’s Noam Brown on multi-agent systems, what math progress implies for recursive self-improvement, and how to tell if models are actually aligned before RSI.

Watch: https://youtu.be/6AgOfiZOWiY

Episode: https://www.dwarkesh.com/p/noam-brown

items.title: Michael Arndt: Oscar-Winning Writer Teaches Storytelling (How I Write)
items.description:
David Perell with screenwriter Michael Arndt on Pixar’s story craft, what separates a weak script from a strong one, and how to diagnose structure when a story stalls.

Watch: https://youtu.be/gi3xYwX7PN4

Episode: https://howiwrite.substack.com/p/michael-arndt-oscar-winning-writer

items.title: 898: An Argument (This American Life)
items.description:
This American Life revisits Nikole Hannah-Jones’s argument about choosing a public school for her daughter — and what happens when the child who lived that choice gets to answer back.

Episode: https://www.thisamericanlife.org/898/an-argument

items.title: Archive: Rosalind Franklin (In Our Time)
items.description:
Melvyn Bragg and guests on Rosalind Franklin — the X-ray crystallography behind the DNA double helix, and how credit for the discovery was divided after her death.

Episode: https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p0p2dn1j

items.title: 708. The Terror: The Reign of Robespierre (Part 2) (The Rest Is History)
items.description:
Tom and Dominic on Robespierre’s Reign of Terror: how revolutionary virtue hardened into emergency rule, denunciation, and the machinery that consumed its own coalition.

Watch: https://youtu.be/5u2SLaHzwZA

items.title: How to Make a Difference: Part 1 (Hidden Brain)
items.description:
Hidden Brain with Martin Seligman on learned helplessness and explanatory style — how the story you tell about a setback can freeze agency or reopen it.

Episode: https://www.hiddenbrain.org/podcast/how-to-make-a-difference-part-1/

items.title: Episode #189 ... Everything that connects us is slowly disappearing. - Byung Chul Han pt. 2 (Philosophize This!)
items.description:
Stephen West on Byung-Chul Han, part two: rituals, truth, community, and public space thinning out — and why resisting total optimization still matters.

Watch: https://youtu.be/JXGvIGqZSuI

Episode: https://philosophizethis.libsyn.com/episode-189-everything-that-connects-us-is-slowly-disappearing-byung-chul-han-pt-2

items.title: 368 | Elizabeth Alexander on Why Democracy Needs Imagination (Sean Carroll's Mindscape)
items.description:
Sean Carroll talks with poet Elizabeth Alexander about literature, close reading, and why imagination is civic infrastructure for democracy.

Watch: https://youtu.be/u-_nDjjD7jE

Episode: https://preposterousuniverse.com/podcast/2026/09/21/368-elizabeth-alexander-on-why-democracy-needs-imagination/

items.title: The Art of True Happiness | Dr. Arthur Brooks (Huberman Lab)
items.description:
Andrew Huberman with Arthur Brooks on happiness as enjoyment, satisfaction, and meaning — a practical frame for measuring a life, not chasing a mood.

Watch: https://youtu.be/Gk2ArbsrZwE

Episode: https://www.hubermanlab.com/episode/the-art-of-true-happiness-arthur-brooks

items.title: The Death of Reading (with James Marriott) (EconTalk)
items.description:
Russ Roberts with James Marriott on deep reading as civilizational infrastructure — patience, abstraction, and the private mind — and what thins when the feed replaces the page.

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-death-of-reading-with-james-marriott/id135066958?i=1000790919027

items.title: 707. The Terror: An Assassination in Paris (Part 1) (The Rest Is History)
items.description:
The Rest Is History on the murder of Marat: how factional rhetoric tipped into the Terror, and political storytelling manufactured bloodlust in revolutionary Paris.

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/707-the-terror-an-assassination-in-paris-part-1/id1537788786

items.title: Episode #252 ... Slaughterhouse-Five - Kurt Vonnegut (Philosophize This!)
items.description:
Philosophize This! on Vonnegut’s Slaughterhouse-Five — war stories that distort war, trauma that fractures time and identity, and why Billy Pilgrim reaches for Tralfamadorian fatalism.

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/episode-252-slaughterhouse-five-kurt-vonnegut/id659155419?i=1000786665460

items.title: 366 | Jim Al-Khalili on Time, Quantum, Biology, and Cosmology (Sean Carroll's Mindscape: Science, Society, Philosophy, Culture, Arts, and Ideas)
items.show: Sean Carroll's Mindscape: Science, Society, Philosophy, Culture, Arts, and Ideas
items.description:
Sean Carroll with physicist Jim Al-Khalili on time: whether it is fundamental or emergent, why it has an arrow, and how physics meets lived experience of its passage.

Watch: https://youtu.be/JVJP_d9U8Gs

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/366-jim-al-khalili-on-time-quantum-biology-and-cosmology/id1406534739?i=1000786961179

items.title: The Home Depot (Acquired)
items.description:
Acquired on Home Depot’s founding: Bernie Marcus and Arthur Blank, fired from a hardware chain, building the no-frills warehouse model that became the best-performing S&P 500 stock since IPO.

Watch: https://youtu.be/6Kq5e49MD6U

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-home-depot/id1050462261?i=1000789467893&uo=4

items.title: Francine Prose: This Is What a Harvard Writing Masterclass Feels Like | How I Write (How I Write)
items.description:
David Perell with Francine Prose on reading like a writer — words, sentences, character, and detail — and how studying books that endure sharpens your own prose.

Watch: https://youtu.be/OuHJ_DW9SnQ

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/francine-prose-this-is-what-a-harvard-writing/id1700171470?i=1000790031658

items.title: #433 How Michael Bloomberg Works (Founders)
items.description:
David Senra on Michael Bloomberg’s working system: attention architecture, information diet, and how Bloomberg built a terminal empire from operator habits.

Watch: https://youtu.be/1iH5YpzPZi8

Episode: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/433-how-michael-bloomberg-works/id1141877104?i=1000789605191
